newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA'S BREAD WHEAT SUPPLIES END IN 20 DAYS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA'S BREAD WHEAT SUPPLIES END IN 20 DAYS.

text.p: Bulgaria's bread wheat supplies will end in the next 15 to 20 days and the cash-strapped caretaker government is considering options for grain imports to stave off a complete grain shortage.

"If Bulgaria imports wheat at current international prices, the price of one kilogram of bread should rise to some 1,800-2,000 levs (from 250 levs now)," agriculture minister Roumen Hristov told reporters on Monday.
Bread being the core of crisis-ridden Bulgarians' meal is subsidised by the government.
Bulgaria will need some $20 million monthly for grain imports, which in the current financial crisis will be difficult to provide, Hristov told reporters.

Bulgaria is battling an acute grain shortage after uncontrolled exports two years ago depleted supplies. Poor harvest last year was attributed to bad weather conditions and lack of funds for fertilisers.
One of the options being discussed was to export cooking oil in return for some 5,000 tonnes of wheat, said Hristov declining to elaborate.
Another possibility is to import 250,000-300,000 tonnes of wheat against a futures contract to export the same quantity of wheat from the new crop.
Bulgaria's state reserve currently holds only 30 percent of its usual supplies, said director of the state marshal time reserve Plamen Dimitrov.

A deal to sell abroad 10,000 tonnes of non-ferrous metals like zinc, nickel and lead from the state reserve and use the cash to buy grain fell through on allegations of unfair tender results, said Dimitrov. He gave no further details.
The cartaker government, in office since last week, hopes to win funding from the European Union and other international lenders and governments, Hristov said.
